transcript.text: On behalf of LP Clubs, I’d like to welcome you all here today.
transcript.speaker: SANDY

transcript.text: My name’s Sandy Fisher and I’m one of the fitness managers here.
transcript.speaker: SANDY

transcript.text: Before we start our tour of the club I’ll just run through some basic information about the facilities we have here, including recent improvements, and explain the types of membership available.
transcript.speaker: SANDY

transcript.text: Our greatest asset is probably our swimming pool which at 25 metres isn’t Olympic-sized, but now we’ve expanded it to eight lanes, it’s much wider.
transcript.speaker: SANDY

transcript.text: This means there are rarely more than a couple of people at a time in each lane.
transcript.speaker: SANDY

transcript.text: Unfortunately, there isn’t space for an outdoor pool here but the glass roof on the swimming pool is partly retractable, which means you can enjoy something of the open-air experience on warmer days.
transcript.speaker: SANDY

transcript.text: Our recently refurbished fitness suite has all the latest exercise equipment including ten new running machines, and a wide range of weight-training machines.
transcript.speaker: SANDY

transcript.text: Each member is given full training in how to operate the equipment and there is always a trainer on duty to offer help and advice.
transcript.speaker: SANDY

transcript.text: Although we do have adult-only times after 6 and at certain times at weekends, children are well catered for.
transcript.speaker: SANDY

transcript.text: Older children continue to benefit from a wide range of tuition; anything from trampolining to yoga.
transcript.speaker: SANDY

transcript.text: One thing all our members appreciate about us is that we take very good care of them.
transcript.speaker: SANDY

transcript.text: This starts on day one with your personal assessment.
transcript.speaker: SANDY

transcript.text: You are asked to fill in a questionnaire giving details of any health problems.
transcript.speaker: SANDY

transcript.text: One of our personal trainers will then go through this with you.
transcript.speaker: SANDY

transcript.text: The trainer will then take you through the safety rules for using the equipment in the fitness suite.
transcript.speaker: SANDY

transcript.text: During your next exercise session a personal trainer will work with you to make sure you understand these.
transcript.speaker: SANDY

transcript.text: It’s very important to do this because we really do want to avoid having any sports injuries.
transcript.speaker: SANDY

transcript.text: There’s a lot more to looking after yourself than simply lifting weights!
transcript.speaker: SANDY

transcript.text: At the end of the personal assessment, the trainer will draw up a plan, outlining what you should try to achieve within a six-week period.
transcript.speaker: SANDY

transcript.text: This will then be reviewed at the end of the six weeks.
transcript.speaker: SANDY

transcript.text: Now, I’ll just quickly run through the types of membership we have available.
transcript.speaker: SANDY

transcript.text: All members must pay a joining fee of £90 in addition to the rates for the monthly membership fees.
transcript.speaker: SANDY

transcript.text: Gold membership entitles you to free entry at all LP Clubs.
transcript.speaker: SANDY

transcript.text: There are now LP clubs in all major cities and towns so if you travel a lot will be a great advantage.
transcript.speaker: SANDY

transcript.text: Individual gold membership costs £50 a month and joint membership for you and your partner will cost £75.
transcript.speaker: SANDY

transcript.text: Premier membership is for professional people whose work commitments make it difficult for them to use the club during the day and so LP gives booking preferences to Premier members at peak times.
transcript.speaker: SANDY

transcript.text: This means you will find it easier to book the sessions at times that suit you.
transcript.speaker: SANDY

transcript.text: Reciprocal arrangements with other LP Clubs are available to Premier members.
transcript.speaker: SANDY

transcript.text: Premier membership is for individuals only, but you will be sent passes for guests every month.
transcript.speaker: SANDY

transcript.text: The monthly fee is £65.
transcript.speaker: SANDY

transcript.text: You don’t have to have any special clothes or equipment when you visit the club.
transcript.speaker: SANDY

transcript.text: We provide robes and hairdryers in the changing rooms, but it’s very important to remember your photo card because you won’t be able to get in without it.
transcript.speaker: SANDY

transcript.text: For people who aren’t working during the day then …

transcript.text: Erm … hello Professor, I’m John Wishart.
transcript.speaker: JOHN

transcript.text: I’m working on my entry for the Global Design Competition.
transcript.speaker: JOHN

transcript.text: My tutor said you might be able to help me with it.
transcript.speaker: JOHN

transcript.text: Ah, yes, I got a copy of your drawings.
transcript.speaker: PROFESSOR

transcript.text: Come in and tell me about it.
transcript.speaker: PROFESSOR

transcript.text: What sort of competition is it?
transcript.speaker: PROFESSOR

transcript.text: Well, it’s an international design competition and we have to come up with a new design for a typical domestic kitchen appliance.
transcript.speaker: JOHN

transcript.text: I see, and are there any special conditions?
transcript.speaker: PROFESSOR

transcript.text: Does it have to save energy for example?
transcript.speaker: PROFESSOR

transcript.text: Actually that was the focus in last year’s competition.
transcript.speaker: JOHN

transcript.text: This year’s different.
transcript.speaker: JOHN

transcript.text: We have to adopt an innovative approach to existing technology, using it in a way that hasn’t been thought of before.
transcript.speaker: JOHN

transcript.text: I see, that sounds tricky.
transcript.speaker: PROFESSOR

transcript.text: And what kitchen appliance have you chosen?
transcript.speaker: PROFESSOR

transcript.text: Well, they’re an everyday kitchen appliance in most Australian houses but they’re all pretty boring and almost identical to each other.
transcript.speaker: JOHN

transcript.text: I think some people will be prepared to pay a little extra for something that looks different.
transcript.speaker: JOHN

transcript.text: That’s a nice idea.
transcript.speaker: PROFESSOR

transcript.text: I see you’ve called your design ‘the Rockpool’; why is that?
transcript.speaker: PROFESSOR

transcript.text: Basically because it looks like the rock pools you find on a beach.
transcript.speaker: JOHN

transcript.text: The top is made of glass so that you can look down into it.
transcript.speaker: JOHN

transcript.text: And there’s a stone at the bottom.
transcript.speaker: PROFESSOR

transcript.text: Is that just for decoration?
transcript.speaker: PROFESSOR

transcript.text: Actually it does have a function.
transcript.speaker: JOHN

transcript.text: Instead of pushing a button, you turn the stone.
transcript.speaker: JOHN

transcript.text: So it’s really just a novel way of starting the dishwasher.
transcript.speaker: PROFESSOR

transcript.text: That’s right.
transcript.speaker: JOHN

transcript.text: It’s a really nice design, but what makes it innovative?
transcript.speaker: PROFESSOR

transcript.text: Well, I decided to make a dishwasher that uses carbon dioxide.
transcript.speaker: JOHN

transcript.text: In place of water and detergent?
transcript.speaker: PROFESSOR

transcript.text: How will you manage that?
transcript.speaker: PROFESSOR

transcript.text: The idea is to pressurize the carbon dioxide so that it becomes a liquid.
transcript.speaker: JOHN

transcript.text: The fluid is then released into the dishwasher where it cleans the dishes all by itself.
transcript.speaker: JOHN

transcript.text: Sounds like a brilliant idea!
transcript.speaker: PROFESSOR

transcript.text: Your system will totally do away with the need for strong detergents.
transcript.speaker: PROFESSOR

transcript.text: So what happens once the dishes are clean?
transcript.speaker: PROFESSOR

transcript.text: Well, to allow them to dry, the liquid carbon dioxide and the waste materials all go to an area called the holding chamber.
transcript.speaker: JOHN

transcript.text: That’s where the liquid is depressurised and so it reverts to a gas.
transcript.speaker: JOHN

transcript.text: Then the oil and grease are separated out and sent to the waste system.
transcript.speaker: JOHN

transcript.text: It sounds like you’ve thought it all out very thoroughly.
transcript.speaker: PROFESSOR

transcript.text: So, what happens to the carbon dioxide once the process is complete?
transcript.speaker: PROFESSOR

transcript.text: Not wasted I hope.
transcript.speaker: PROFESSOR

transcript.text: Actually, that’s where the real savings are made.
transcript.speaker: JOHN

transcript.text: The carbon dioxide is sent back to the cylinder and can be used again and again.
transcript.speaker: JOHN

transcript.text: What a terrific idea.
transcript.speaker: PROFESSOR

transcript.text: Do you think it will ever be built?
transcript.speaker: PROFESSOR

transcript.text: Probably not, but that’s OK.
transcript.speaker: JOHN

transcript.text: Well, I’m sure a lot of positive things will come out of your design.
transcript.speaker: PROFESSOR

transcript.text: Now, you seem to have thought about everything so what exactly did you need me to help you with?
transcript.speaker: PROFESSOR

transcript.text: Well, my design has made it to the final stage of the competition and, in a few months’ time.
transcript.speaker: JOHN

transcript.text: I have to give a presentation, and that’s the part I was hoping you could help me with.
transcript.speaker: JOHN

transcript.text: Right, well that should be easy enough.
transcript.speaker: PROFESSOR

transcript.text: What have you managed to do so far?
transcript.speaker: PROFESSOR

transcript.text: Well, I’ve got detailed drawings to show how it will work and I’ve also written a 500-word paper on it.
transcript.speaker: JOHN

transcript.text: I see.
transcript.speaker: PROFESSOR

transcript.text: Well, if you want to stand a good chance of winning you really need a model of the machine.
transcript.speaker: PROFESSOR

transcript.text: Yes, I thought I might but I’m having a few problems.
transcript.speaker: JOHN

transcript.text: What is the main difficulty so far?
transcript.speaker: PROFESSOR

transcript.text: Let me guess – is it the materials?
transcript.speaker: PROFESSOR

transcript.text: Yes.
transcript.speaker: JOHN

transcript.text: I want it to look professional but everything that’s top quality is also very expensive.
transcript.speaker: JOHN

transcript.text: Look, projects like this are very important to us.
transcript.speaker: PROFESSOR

transcript.text: They really help lift our profile.
transcript.speaker: PROFESSOR

transcript.text: So why don’t you talk to the university about a grant?
transcript.speaker: PROFESSOR

transcript.text: I can help you fill out the application forms if you like.
transcript.speaker: PROFESSOR

transcript.text: That would be a great.
transcript.speaker: JOHN

transcript.text: You’d better show me this paper you’ve written as well.
transcript.speaker: PROFESSOR

transcript.text: For a global competition such as this you need to make sure the technical details you’ve given are accurate and thorough.
transcript.speaker: PROFESSOR

transcript.text: That would be a great help.
transcript.speaker: JOHN

transcript.text: Is there anything else I can do?
transcript.speaker: PROFESSOR

transcript.text: Well, I’m really …
transcript.speaker: JOHN

transcript.text: Today we continue our series on ecology and conservation with a look at a particularly endangered member of the black bear family.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: One in ten black bears is actually born with a white coat, which is the result of a special gene that surfaces in a few.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: Local people have named it ‘the spirit bear’.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: And according to the legends of these communities, its snowy fur brings with it a special power.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: Because of this, it has always been highly regarded by them – so much that they do not speak of seeing it to anyone else.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: It is their way of protecting it when strangers visit the area.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: The white bear’s habitat is quite interesting.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: The bear’s strong relationship with the old-growth rainforest is a complex one.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: The white bear relies on the huge centuries-old trees in the forest in many ways.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: For example, the old-growth trees have extremely long roots that help prevent erosion of the soil along the banks of the many fish streams.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: Keeping these banks intact is important because these streams are home to salmon, which are the bear’s main food source.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: In return, the bear’s feeding habits nurture the forest.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: As the bears eat the salmon, they discard the skin and bones in great amounts on the forest floor, which provide vital nutrients.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: These produce lush vegetation that sustains thousands of other types of life forms, from birds to insects and more.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: Today, the spirit bear lives off the coast of the province of British Columbia on a few islands.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: There is great concern for their survival since it is estimated that less than two hundred of these white bears remain.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: The best way to protect them is to make every effort to preserve the delicate balance of their forest environment – in other words, their ecosystem.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: The greatest threat to the bear’s existence is the loss of its habitat.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: Over many years, logging companies have stripped the land by cutting down a large number of trees.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: In addition, they have built roads which have fractured the areas where the bear usually feeds, and many hibernation sites have also been lost.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: The logging of the trees along the streams has damaged the places where the bears fish.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: To make matters worse, the number of salmon in those streams is declining because there is no legal limit on fishing at the moment.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: all these influences have a negative impact on the spirit bear’s very existence, which is made all the more fragile by the fact that reproduction among these bears has always been disappointingly low.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: And so, what’s the situation going forward?
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: Community organizations, environmental groups and the British Columbia government are now working together on the problem.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: The government is now requiring logging companies to adopt a better logging method, which is a positive step.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: However, these measures alone may not be sufficient to ensure a healthy population of the spirit bear in the future.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: Other steps also need to be taken.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: While it is important to maintain the spirit bear’s habitat, there also needs to be more emphasis on its expansion.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: The move is justified as it will also create space for other bears that are losing their homes …
transcript.speaker: LECTURER
